title: Vehicle Checks & Tyres
whatItIs: You MUST make sure your vehicle is legal and roadworthy. Regular checks of tyres, lights, fluids and warning displays help.

keyFacts.text: Car tyres MUST have at least 1.6 mm of tread across the central three-quarters, all the way round.
Tyres MUST be correctly inflated to the maker's specification for the load being carried.
Lights, indicators, reflectors and number plates MUST be kept clean and clear.
Windscreens and windows MUST be kept clean and clear.

keyFacts: Check tyre pressures when the tyres are cold, using the figures in the handbook.

items.title: P · Petrol
items.text: Enough fuel or charge for your journey, especially on motorways.

items.title: O · Oil
items.text: Check fluid levels, including oil, at least weekly. Know your low-fluid warning lights.

items.title: W · Water
items.text: Engine coolant and screen washer topped up.

items.title: D · Damage
items.text: Check for fuel leaks and any damage to the fuel cap or tank.

items.title: E · Electrics
items.text: Lights, indicators, horn and warning lights all working.

items.title: R · Rubber
items.text: Tyres: tread, pressure, cuts and bulges. Wiper blades too.

b.label: Uneven tyre wear
points: May be a brake or suspension fault

onTheTest.question: What is the legal minimum tread depth for car tyres?
onTheTest.why: Car tyres must have at least 1.6 mm of tread across the central three-quarters of the tread, all the way round.

traps: 1.6 mm is across the central three-quarters, all the way round the tyre.
Check pressures when the tyres are cold.
Good tread isn't enough: tyres should also be free from cuts and other defects.

review.checkedAgainst: Official text on gov.uk — The Highway Code: Annex 6 (Vehicle maintenance, safety and security); The Highway Code: Rule 97 (Before setting off)
